key_insight: Known weak-bit locations are worth far more than their storage: herded into one RS symbol, 8 mapped weak bits cost one symbol, cutting codeword failure ~1e-2 to ~1e-14 at 1e-3.
killer_doubt: The same pointer map (8 x 9 b = 72 b/line, 14%) lets ECP-style replacement fix known bits without spending ECC. VRT cells missed by boot maps still escape.
decisive_experiment: FPGA DDR5 retention profiling (~$60k): map weak cells at 1 s and 4 s, 85 C, over two weeks. Measure the share of failures absent from the boot map (VRT); compare herding, ECP and erasure decoding.
prior_art: ECP error-correcting pointers (Schechter, ISCA 2010); ArchShield fault-map replication (Nair, ISCA 2013); Bamboo ECC symbol alignment (Kim, HPCA 2015); from memory.

key_insight: Winding packages square metres of thin-film array into cm3 with no tiers or TSVs, and Schoop end-face spraying is a proven mass-contact method.
killer_doubt: Winding adds no bits: every turn needs its full patterned area. R2R TFT at ~1 um gives ~16-20 GB/m2; at $50-150/m2 that is $2.5-9/GB versus DDR5 $1.48/GB.
decisive_experiment: Wind a 20-turn polyimide tape carrying 10k IGZO 1T1C cells (~$150k, university sheet/R2R line). Measure end-face contact yield per turn at 25 um radial pitch, and Ioff and Vt shift after winding.
prior_art: Film-capacitor winding and Schoop metallization (standard); HP self-aligned imprint lithography for R2R TFTs; our I-07604 rolled array and I-05241 web-line memory (both DROP).

key_insight: Correcting with write-back on every refresh pass, not only on read, stops transient flips (VRT, hammer, SEU) from pairing up inside one codeword.
killer_doubt: Toom erosion is proven only for repetition codes (rate ~0). Static weak cells re-fail every pass, so code strength sets tolerable BER; 2D checks need adjacent rows open together.
decisive_experiment: Monte Carlo (~$20k) on measured FPGA retention/VRT maps: local Toom-style 2D code versus BCH on 1 KB (Hi-ECC) at equal parity, 1 s and 4 s refresh. Kill if the local code needs >2x parity.
prior_art: Hi-ECC (Wilkerson, ISCA 2010) and Morphable ECC (Chou, 2015) use strong ECC for ~1 s refresh; DDR5 ECS in-DRAM scrub; Toom rule (1980), from memory.

key_insight: Comparing stored check bits with a predicted value's check bits is a cheap equality test: a confirmed line costs ~80 bits up, 1 bit down, ignoring decayed data cells.
killer_doubt: Only zero lines (~5-20% of reads) are predictable without a line-sized copy, which is a cache; zero-line metadata skips DRAM entirely. AI weight and KV streams are unpredictable.
decisive_experiment: gem5/Ramulator trace study (~$30k): share of DRAM reads equal to zero, last-evicted value or a stride prediction for SPEC, graph and LLM decode; net energy including 80-bit uplinks and mispredicted double accesses.
prior_art: Zero-content augmented caches (Dusser 2009); LCP compression with zero-line metadata (Pekhimenko 2013); load value prediction (Lipasti 1996); RFVP approximate value prediction; from memory.

key_insight: Orthogonal spreading does turn one dead cell into small distributed noise, the graceful-degradation property used in CDMA and phase-coded holographic storage.
killer_doubt: Walsh coefficients of 64 bits span +/-8 bit-amplitudes (65 levels): cells need ~7-bit analog SNR for 1 bit/cell. A rail-stuck cell shifts every bit ~1 amplitude; Hamming costs 11%.
decisive_experiment: Simulation using measured IGZO gain-cell or FeFET level noise and drift (~$20k): BER of Walsh-64 spreading versus binary cells plus BCH at equal cell count, with 1e-3 stuck-at-rail and mid-scale failures.
prior_art: Real-number DFT/analog error-correcting codes (Wolf 1983, Marshall 1984); Hadamard phase-coded holographic storage; our I-08644 rotation (DROP); from memory.

key_insight: Pairwise lot splits give a cheap, continuously updated chamber ranking, so depreciated chambers can be steered to tolerant layers instead of retired.
killer_doubt: Fabs already run commonality analysis and chamber matching on full wafer histories; Elo discards effect size and confounds 500+ steps. Mature DRAM yields ~85-90% leave only ~1-3% to win.
decisive_experiment: Retrospective study on one partner fab's MES and bit-fail data (~$200k, under NDA): Elo ranking versus mixed-effects commonality models for predicting chamber-attributable yield loss on held-out lots.
prior_art: Tool commonality and chamber-matching analytics (PDF Solutions Exensio, KLA Klarity, Applied E3) are standard in fabs; Bradley-Terry pairwise ranking; from memory.

key_insight: Cycle clearing can match form-factor and speed-bin mismatches that bilateral trades miss, without anyone revealing a cash price.
killer_doubt: Kidney exchange exists because money is banned; DRAM has liquid spot markets and brokers. It creates zero bits; even 5-10% mismatched inventory clears once, worth weeks of supply.
decisive_experiment: Survey 20 OEMs, ODMs and distributors (~$50k) for mismatched DRAM inventory by SKU; run cycle clearing offline and measure what clears beyond what spot brokers already move.
prior_art: DRAMeXchange spot market, independent brokers and distributor buy-backs; kidney paired exchange (Roth et al.); B2B barter exchanges; from memory.

key_insight: Holding WIP at a configurable pre-bond stage is classic postponement; paired with prepaid capacity options it could fund countercyclical capacity without a new fab.
killer_doubt: Bits live in the tier wafers, which still need ~3 months of front-end; stockpiling them is inventory. Bonded multi-tier DRAM does not exist, and stored bond surfaces need re-CMP.
decisive_experiment: Store 25 hybrid-bond-ready Cu/SiCN wafers for 0, 3, 6 and 12 months under N2; bond to fresh wafers and measure void density and contact-chain yield (~$300k with a bonding foundry).
prior_art: HP Procurement Risk Management option contracts for memory (Nagali 2008); memory-maker die and wafer banks; hyperscaler LTA prepayments; HP postponement; from memory.

key_insight: Spending large, trimmed sense amplifiers only where ECC flags doubt is NAND read-retry logic applied to DRAM activation.
killer_doubt: Minimum latches have sigma-Vt ~60 mV against a ~70 mV signal (~10% errors). Whole-row ECC before restore, and muxing 8k bitlines to pooled amplifiers, add area, delay and Cbl.
decisive_experiment: SPICE plus 28 nm MPW (~$200k): 256 bitlines with minimum isolated latches and 4 pooled trimmed amplifiers; measure first-pass error rate, re-sense success after a 5 ns ECC delay, and energy per activation.
prior_art: Offset-cancellation sense amps (Samsung OCSA); NAND read-retry; restore truncation (Zhang, HPCA 2016); SRAM double sensing; from memory.

key_insight: Subthreshold current does scale with 1-exp(-Vds/kT); a bootstrapped midpoint held within ~0.5 mV of the storage node would cut it ~50x.
killer_doubt: The Si tail is GIDL/GIJL to the body, set by gate-drain field, not Vds. ~20 mV follower mismatch leaves 1-exp(-0.65) = 0.5, only ~2x. IGZO already gives <1 aA.
decisive_experiment: 28 nm MPW eDRAM macro (~$150k): bootstrapped 3T versus 1T1C cells, 1 Mb retention maps at 85 C. Kill if the 1e-6 tail gains <10x at <1.5x area with zero static bias.
prior_art: Electrometer guard driving (classic); bootstrapped eDRAM gain cells; our I-02778 equipotential guard (DROP, same mechanism); Kioxia OCTRAM IGZO <1 aA.

key_insight: In-situ junction gates have no oxide, interface traps or PBTI, and skip conformal high-k/metal in 100-tier lateral cavities. Boron moves only ~2 nm at 700 C for 10 h.
killer_doubt: Off-state needs p+ gates ~1.5-2 V reverse to the storage node: ~0.8-1.5 MV/cm junction fields, the TAT/BTBT physics behind the 13 fA tail. Blanket p+ sheets still need per-wordline slits.
decisive_experiment: Grow a 4-tier Si/SiGe stack with in-situ p+ sublayers (~$400k, university epi plus e-beam); build 30 nm lateral JFETs; map Ioff of 10k devices at 85 C hold bias. Advance if the 1e-4 tail is <1 fA.
prior_art: Junctionless transistors (Colinge 2010); JFET capacitorless-DRAM proposals (from memory, unverified); imec Si/SiGe 3D DRAM stacks; no epitaxial-JFET 3D DRAM found.

key_insight: Clamp the bitline, sense a short plate strip: 1 fF into ~3.7 fF gives ~135 mV versus ~14 mV on 35 fF; restore drives the ~2 fF strip, not bitlines.
killer_doubt: One sense amp per 8-cell strip cannot fit; selector routing to shared amplifiers re-adds ~10-20 fF of vertical line at 100 tiers unless each strip gets a gain FET.
decisive_experiment: SPICE with extracted 3D parasitics, then a 2-tier planar-emulation MPW (~$250k): 8-64-cell strips with a local gain FET; measure signal, unselected-cell disturb after 1e9 plate excursions, and energy per activation.
prior_art: Micron dynamic cell-plate sensing, divided plate lines paired with bitlines, US 5,991,216 and US 8,009,460 (via search snippet); FeRAM plate-line drive.
